cohort: 24,843 women with term, livebirth, singleton pregnancies with spontaneous or induced labor who delivered at the San Paolo Hospital from 1996 through 2019
finding: Multiparous women aged 40 years or older, regardless of labor type, had a two-fold increased risk of cesarean section compared to women aged 25-29 years.
mod_finding: The study examined cesarean section rates across different age groups and Robson groups, which classify pregnancies based on factors including parity and labor onset.
